html:
The war after the presidential runoff of 28 November 2010, when Laurent Gbagbo refused to accept the victory of Alassane Ouattara that the electoral commission and the United Nations had confirmed.

For four months both men claimed to be president. Fighting in Abidjan and the west killed about 3,000 people; hundreds died in a massacre at Duekoue. Ouattara's forces swept south, and with French and UN support they captured Gbagbo on 11 April 2011. He was tried at the International Criminal Court and acquitted in 2019. Ouattara has ruled since. See also the first civil war.
